correctness.rationale: The one-node normalized Lanczos estimator is derived from the Rayleigh quotient. Constant sign output gives exact squared bias. Absolute convergence of the circular logarithm Fourier expansion and orthogonality give spherical mean, variance and dilogarithmic MSE. The risk-difference derivative has a strictly increasing numerator crossing from -1 to 2 log 2; combined with H(0)=0 and H(1-)=+infinity this proves one unique interior reversal. A standalone checker supplies independent exact rational bounds and finite angular quadrature diagnostics, with no claim that finite testing proves the theorem.

Standard probe laws and classical Fourier series are prior tools, not novelty. Priority risk of uninspected specialized calculation remains.

value.rationale: One matrix-vector-product logdet quadrature is a meaningful limiting computational budget. Even when Rademacher sampling has zero randomness on the diagonal model, its deterministic log-Jensen quadrature bias can exceed the bias-plus-variance of a spherical probe. The theorem isolates this unexpected error trade-off with complete sharp conditioning classification and explicit risk law. This is a motivated structural boundary, not a numerical table recomputation or a universal performance claim.
